interest: This docket sheet illustrates pre-World War II strategic anxieties in Southeast Asia, highlighting American diplomatic monitoring of suspected Japanese naval espionage and submarine movements during Dutch fleet maneuvers in the Netherlands East Indies. It also provides valuable archival provenance, showing how intelligence on clandestine foreign naval activities was indexed, tracked, and cross-referenced to related State Department files (811.33/544).
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet (File No. 894.3356D) concerning visits of Japanese vessels and aircraft to ports of the Netherlands East Indies. The index records a single communication, Despatch No. 927 dated November 16, 1937, from American Consul Walter A. Foote in Batavia, regarding the possible presence of Japanese submarines in the waters of the Netherlands Indies during maneuvers of the Netherlands Fleet, which was cross-referenced and filed under 811.33/544.

subfiles.summary: This 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexes correspondence under decimal file 894.3356D concerning visits of Japanese vessels to the Dutch East Indies. It records a single entry for Despatch No. 927 of November 16, 1937, sent by Walter A. Foote from Batavia. The purport notes reports on the possible presence of Japanese submarines in Netherlands Indies waters during maneuvers of the Netherlands Fleet, directing researchers to cross-reference file 811.33/544.
